items.title: Continuous crossings
items.body:
**Use case**
When a footway/path meets a road, the user is asked: "Is there a crossing here?" The answer options are:
* Yes (e.g. the kerb is lowered here or there are markings)
* No, but crossing is possible
* No, crossing is prohibited or impossible

A scenario not covered by the above options is a "continuous footway", "continuous sidewalk", "continuous pavement", "continuous crossing" or "Copenhagen crossing" (it goes by many names):
![Ryland_Road_continuous_footway](https://github.com/streetcomplete/StreetComplete/assets/127188803/ea398aaa-98a8-491d-aabb-60c884d8d26c)

At least in one case a mapper was asked the StreetComplete quest for this type of situation and answered "No, but crossing is possible". It's understandable why they chose this option, but it results in tagging `crossing=informal` which is not right at all.

**Proposed Solution**
We now have an approved tag [`crossing:continuous=yes`](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:crossing:continuous) for the above situation. 

I suggest adding a fourth option to the question "Is there a crossing here?"
* Yes (e.g. the kerb is lowered here or there are markings)
* No, but crossing **the road** is possible (-> slight tweak to the wording)
* No, crossing is prohibited or impossible
* **The path just continues uninterrupted across the road.**

Selecting the new option should set `crossing:continuous=yes`.

Other options for phrasing it:
* "Yes, it is a continuous crossing [sidewalk/pavement/cycleway]" (though that assumes that mappers are familiar with the term)
* "Yes, but drivers have to cross a section of footway [cycleway], instead of pedestrians [cyclists] having to cross the road"

The exact phrasing could maybe depend on the tagging of the path (e.g. if it's a footway or cycleway or shared), to make sure it's clear. (It's clearer to say "The sidewalk just continues uninterrupted" than to say "The path...")

Because the situation is much more common with sidewalks than elsewhere, another soluation might be to only show the fourth option for paths, footways and cycleways with tags such as `footway=sidewalk` and `is_sidepath`.

items.title: Add detail to crossing sound signals and vibration changeset message
items.body:
When the traffic signals sound and traffic signals vibration quests are answered the comment on the changeset is 
"Add traffic_signals:vibration tag", e.g. https://www.openstreetmap.org/changeset/99294493
Or "Add traffic_signals:sound tag", e.g. https://www.openstreetmap.org/changeset/99263090

All other quests (I think) have more meaningful comments, e.g. "Add whether pedestrian crossing has an island" (https://www.openstreetmap.org/changeset/99305683) etc.

(All changesets are just random recent ones I found through OSMCha).

How about "Add whether traffic signals have sound signals" and "Add whether traffic signals have tactile indication that it's safe to cross".

I'm up for fixing this (easy change, but I want to contribute).

Also related, is there a reason for changeset comments not being localised? If it's an enhancement that's wanted then I'll open a different issue for it.

items.title: Show geometry for crossing quests
items.body:
I noticed that sometimes people confuse crossings with other nearby crossings.
See https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/8615277295 and https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/6557473402 which both have an incorrect `crossing:island=yes`, likely because there actually is a island at a different nearby crossing.

Showing geometry should help people with identifying the correct crossing.

(I was originally going to suggest not asking for crossings that are not part of a road, but showing geometry should help as well, and in more cases)

items.body:
### General

Affected tag(s) to be modified/added: [crossing:island](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:crossing:island)
Question asked: **Does this crossing have a pedestrian island?**

<!-- If the answer is not obvious, please append a short explanation to each item (or, if it is longer, below), explaining the reason. -->
### Checklist
Checklist for quest suggestions (see guidelines):
- [x] 🚧 To be added tag is established and has a useful purpose ([Taginfo](https://taginfo.openstreetmap.org/keys/?key=crossing%3Aisland) lists 99k items)
- [x] 🤔 Any answer the user can give must have an equivalent tagging (Quest should not reappear to other users when solved by one)
- [x] 🐿️ Easily answerable by everyone from the outside but a survey is necessary 
- [x] 💤 Not an overwhelming percentage of elements have the same answer (No spam): I'm not sure about this one. I think most crossings won't have a pedestrian island, but quite a few do. That might vary by region though.
- [x] 🕓 Applies to a reasonable number of elements (Worth the effort)

### Ideas for implementation

**Element selection:**
`nodes with crossing and crossing != "island" and !crossing:island`

**Proposed GUI:**
Simple Yes / No

### Related

* https://github.com/westnordost/StreetComplete/issues/495 (same quest suggestion, but with the older `crossing=island` tag, which doesn't prevent "no" as an answer to stop the quest from reappearing to other users)
* https://github.com/westnordost/StreetComplete/issues/1637 / https://github.com/westnordost/StreetComplete/commit/a609da8c7f0a51c24f6ca5fdd06b0b361b7cf8ec (include `crossing=island` in crossing quest, and set `crossing:island` to `yes` accordingly)

items.title: Continuous crossings and other traffic calming features on crossings.
items.body:
[Continuous crossings](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:crossing:continuous) are becoming more common and are currently not able to be mapped.

There has already been discussions on this:
In https://github.com/streetcomplete/StreetComplete/issues/5443#issuecomment-1899405931 @osmuser63783 suggested adding them as an option to the "Is there a crossing here?" quest. This was rejected since it is orthagonal to the other options offered by the quest.

Instead I suggest modifying the "Does this crossing have an island?" quest to a radio menu:


---
Does this crossing have features to protect pedestrians?:
- [ ] There is an refuge island. (`crossing:island=yes`).
- [ ] The surface of the sidewalk continues uninterrupted. (`crossing:continuous=yes`)
- [ ] The road is raised to slow vehicles, and allow for safer crossing. (`traffic_calming=table and crossing:continuous=no`)
- [ ] No. (`crossing:island=no`, `crossing:continuous=no`).
---
I would also suggest adding an image option 2 and 3 in the hint box.

Alternatively, this could be implemented as an image quest, the problem I see here is that it might be hard to explain to users what the key elements that they must look out for, are.

items.title: Railroad crossing warning devices
items.body: In the US, railroad crossings with minor streets rarely have gates, and may or may not even have warning devices, especially as you go into more rural areas. (This may also be true around the world and particularly outside Europe; I can only speak to my experience in the US.) Whether these crossings have warning devices is even more relevant than if they have gates. ### General **What warning devices does this crossing have?** - No warning devices - Only lights - Only a bell - Lights and a bell (or **Does this railroad crossing have warning lights?** and **Does this railroad crossing have a bell?** separately) #### Affected tags - On elements: [`railway=crossing`](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag:railway%3Dcrossing) and [`railway=level_crossing`](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag:railway%3Dlevel_crossing) - [`crossing:bell`](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:crossing:bell) to `yes`/`no` - [`crossing:light`](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:crossing:light) to `yes`/`no` ### Checklist Checklist for quest suggestions (see [guidelines](https://github.com/streetcomplete/StreetComplete/blob/master/QUEST_GUIDELINES.md)): - [x] 🚧 To be added tag is established and has a useful purpose - [x] 🤔 Any answer the user can give must have an equivalent tagging (Quest should not reappear to other users when solved by one) - [x] 🐿️ Easily answerable by any pedestrian from the outside but a survey is necessary - One potential problem here is that not all bells may be obvious to the casual observer, e.g. [electronic bells](https://www.youtube.com/watch?Vi3oWGzMZIs) blend in with the post. It may be worth asking *only* about lights. - [x] 💤 Not an overwhelming percentage of quests have the same answer (No spam) - Even in urban areas, there can be a reasonable number of grade crossings with no warning devices. - [x] 🕓 Applies to a reasonable number of map data (Worth the effort) ### Ideas for implementation #### Element selection: - `railway:crossing`, `railway:level_crossing` #### Metadata needed: Per the wiki, this seems like it should be fairly consistent worldwide? #### Proposed UI: The question, of course, could be split into two (as noted above), or could be combined into “does this railroad crossing have lights and a bell”, with “only […]” located in the overflow menu. (And maybe the image should include a crossbuck but I was not feeling like doing that much work in Inkscape.)

items.title: Allow tagging tactile_paving=incorrect for when only one side of a crossing has it
items.body:
**Use case**
It affects also crossing ques, but is `no` really correct when only one side has paving?

_Originally posted by @matkoniecz in https://github.com/streetcomplete/StreetComplete/issues/3762#issuecomment-1039607154_

Probably `incorrect` is the right thing there. The wiki has "or if only one sloped kerb at a crossing has tactile paving" as an example of `incorrect`.

_Originally posted by @arrival-spring in https://github.com/streetcomplete/StreetComplete/issues/3762#issuecomment-1039612736_

OT, but I'd appreciate some clarity/a new option for this (I normally just tag no as it's not yes). Also on a crossing with an island, if its only on either side but not on the island which is right?

_Originally posted by @peternewman in https://github.com/streetcomplete/StreetComplete/issues/3762#issuecomment-1040544178_

There was a bit of a discussion here: https://github.com/streetcomplete/StreetComplete/issues/2738

I'd support having an other answers button of "Tactile paving only at the top or only at the bottom" and similarly for the crossing quest "Tactile paving only on one side" which would tag `incorrect` after a confirmation.

_Originally posted by @arrival-spring in https://github.com/streetcomplete/StreetComplete/issues/3762#issuecomment-1040650287_

See also #2738 .

I appreciate incorrect is low usage currently (0.11%) but I don't know about others but I'd certainly have been tagging no when it's only on one side (given "Does this crosswalk have tactile pavings on both sides?") although I'm not sure how many of those I've had. 

As mentioned I've also been tagging no if it's on the kerbs but not on the island as it's not on both sides of the two crossings, but I appreciate that probably needs a more general tagging discussion to find out what is the "correct" answer, or asking a blind person. @matkoniecz do you have contacts/feedback from your tactile maps?

**Proposed Solution**
Add an other answer for only on one side of the crossing

items.title: Redundant "tactile paving" quest being asked - both on kerbs and on highway=crossing node

labels.name: wontfix
labels.description: idea rejected because it is out of scope or because required work is not matching expected benefits

items.body:
**Use case**

At some crossings (encountered it multiple times), user is being asked about `tactile_paving` on each side of the crossing individually, and *then again* "if there is tactile paving on both sides". It is confusing and seems redundant.

Example this location: https://www.openstreetmap.org/note/2894360

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/156656/137835934-394a2370-a0d8-456b-b02e-3a05649a4ccb.mp4



**Proposed Solution**

- ideally, user would be asked just one question - if there is `tactile_paving` on both sides, and if there is, two additional individual questions if it exists on each side individually would be skipped (that is, they would automatically solved by that one quest).
- alternatively, if the user is asked for each of the sides if it has tactile paving, asking them again "if it exists on both sides" is redundant and confusing, so it should be removed. 

(this was logged on `SC 36.0-beta2` based my fork, but no changes related to that issues should be in there)

items.title: Quest: type of crossing

labels.name: new quest
labels.description: accepted new quest proposal (if marked as blocked, it may require upstream work first)

items.body:
The basic idea is to look for `nodes with highway=crossing and !crossing` and ask the user to select what kind of crossing it is (https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:crossing):
* `crossing=traffic_signals`
* `crossing=uncontrolled`
* `crossing=island`
* `crossing=unmarked`

Optionally we could also try to handle lack of possibility to cross the street, this would require removal of `highway=crossing` and adding `crossing=no`.

items.title: Don't ask for islands and kerb heights on continuous crossings
items.body:
[Continuous crossings](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:crossing:continuous) are very unlikely to have islands, so this stops StreetComplete asking for them.

Among the ~9k `crossing:continuous=yes`, there are only [22 cases](https://overpass-turbo.eu/s/2ulD) with `crossing:island=yes`. Most of these either don't actually have an island or aren't actually continuous. The only real cases I found are these bicycle crossings in the Netherlands and islands are probably less important when cycling:
- https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/317439715 (note that the parallel pedestrian crossing is not continuous)
- https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/7466006701 (this is a pedestrian crossing that's not actually continuous, but the parallel bicycle one is)

~Not tested locally, it's just a query change.~ Confirmed it works as expected with debug apk.

Motivated by: https://community.openstreetmap.org/t/vorgehen-gegen-das-eintragen-von-nicht-eigenschaften/145808

When asked, "What type of crossing is this?" the options are, "Controlled by traffic lights," "Marked," and, "Without road markings."

items.title: Australia: speed up pedestrian crossings entry
items.body:
**Use case**
Australia uses [a standard pedestrian crossing button](https://www.australiangeographic.com.au/blogs/dr-karl-need-to-know/2016/07/the-pedestrian-button/), which is in place at every pedestrian crossing in the country. It does three things:
1. A button to request a walk signal
2. Sound signals for the blind
3. A tactile indication for when it's safe to cross

This is a standard on every pedestrian crossing in the country, and [known as the PB/5](https://theconversation.com/sublime-design-the-pb-5-pedestrian-button-26232). It replaced previous buttons in place since the 1960s which also had sound signals and tactile indications. (They're quite clever, incorporating a microphone for noise ambience, to make the noises it makes audible over traffic noise).

Currently, within StreetComplete, there are three questions asked by default around pedestrian crossings:
1. Do these traffic lights have a button to request a walk signal?
2. Do these traffic lights have a tactile indication for blind people for when it is safe to cross?
3. Are there sound signals for the blind here?

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/231941/147712288-72ffa5f8-ba78-4392-9e88-291ab117871e.png)

If 1 is true, then automatically 2 and 3 are true. Always. Every single time.

**Issues with the current implementation**

First, it's three questions to answer, rather than one; and second, the availability of the tactile indication isn't very well known by able-bodied people - the help information refers to the rotating cone at the bottom of British crossings, and it could be that users answer this question negatively. The PB/5 features a vibrating touch panel on the front of the unit. In the pictures, it's the bit in the middle of the big tactile arrow.

**Proposed Solution**

Do not bother the user with questions 2 and 3, above. We already know the answer is "yes".

`if
(country="Australia")
and
(these traffic lights have a button to request a walk signal)
then
(these traffic lights have a tactile indication and sound signals)`

**Less good solution**

Amend the help text to read:

_Hint: Often this is a vibrating button or rotating cone on the bottom of the traffic button case, or a touch panel on its front._

items.title: new images for parking lot and unmarked crossing
items.body:
fixes #2897 and addresses #3341 (more space for labels so actual crossing without road markings can be shown)

Crossing photo is not 100% ideal but quite good, better than existing one. I am not planning to invest more time into it, but if someone manages to get one that is

- better in some way
- shows simple crossing (without crossing signs, without island, without road markings - if this things are present on photo it may confuse mapper and make more likely to treat `highway=crossing` as not a crossing)
- without distracting debris or less of it
- still interpretable as crossing (dropped kerb?), walking human would help
- clearly a crossing on road
- with plenty of space for labeling at bottom
- on open license

then feel free to make PR! Or just link photo and I will make a PR.

items.title: Group crossing quests into a single upload changeset
items.body:
We now have a lot of crossing related quests which is great, but this leads to a lot of changesets, which makes it harder for OSMCha reviewers.

Do you think it would make sense to group all of these together into a single changeset, "Updated crossings".

- Add whether traffic signals have a button for pedestrians
- Add traffic_signals:sound tag
- Add traffic_signals:vibration tag
- Add tactile pavings on crosswalks
- Add whether pedestrian crossing has an island
- etc.

items.title: Extend curb quest to highway=crossings without a way

labels.name: wontfix
labels.description: idea rejected because it is out of scope or because required work is not matching expected benefits

items.body:
**Use case**
In my area, most sidewalks are directly connected to the street, not separated by a green strip. So mapping them as individual lines is wrong IMHO.

So crossings are single nodes on the highway, while the sidewalks are tags on the highway.

**Proposed Solution**
Is there a chance to extend the curb-quest to single node crossings as well, with `curb:right/left` or `curb:forward/backward`?

items.title: Reword question for railway crossing - ask specifically about crossing barriers
items.body:
**Use case**
I think that railway crossing barrier quest can have a more clear question. I think that refering specifically to barriers would be useful as crossings can have also other protection - road signs, light signals, sound signal, human presence and so on.

As side effect translation in Polish would become  far less awkward :)

**Proposed Solution**
Current one:

> How is this railway crossing protected?

Proposed:

> How are the barriers set up at this level crossing?

I am pretty sure that it is a bit Engrish and should be reworded
